sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 7:22

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 7:22:1
items.html:
The Noga [brightness] round about it, and corresponding to it likewise in Yetzira, and so in Beria, and so in Atzilut: Indeed know that the ABYA of the shell are the reverse of the ABYA of holiness. For in holiness, whatever is higher is holier, and as it diminishes its holiness descends until the end of Assiya; but in the shells it is the reverse, for the upper shell, which stands opposite Atzilut, is weak and is not so evil, and the further it descends the more the impurity and the shells grow strong.
There is also a distinction in the matter of the mixture of good and evil in the shell of Noga, that is, in the dross that was not sorted. For in Assiya most of it is evil, and there they are the father of the fathers of impurity, namely the impurity of a corpse. And the shells of Yetzira are mixed good and evil, half and half, and it defiles even non-sacred food, for the world of Yetzira is the secret of non-sacred food eaten in purity. And in the shells of Beria the mixture is mostly good and a minority evil, and it defiles only the Teruma, for the world of Beria is Teruma. And the world of Atzilut is mostly good, and there is in it a minority of shell; and even that minority is not mixed with the holiness, and the shell of Atzilut has no impurity in it, but it disqualifies the holy offerings, for Atzilut is holy offerings.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 7:22:2
items.html: “Merachefet [hovering],” whose letters are Met Parach — they are the 288 sparks of the kings who died: That is, the sparks are records of the lights that flew away from the seven kings and died; and the records descended with them so that they would have the strength to rise at the resurrection of the dead. And RAPACH [288] and VaParach [“and it flew away”] have the same letters. And understand.
